# CS 29.927 — Additional tests

> [!summary]
> CS 29.927 sets the additional tests for the rotor drive system of a large
> rotorcraft. It is a CS-29 specification, not a CS-E one, and the rotorcraft
> applicant owns it. Four regimes apply: dynamic and endurance testing, torque
> application tests where the pilot does not control engine output directly, a
> loss-of-lubrication test for each gearbox needed for safe flight, and 50
> overspeed runs. Three of its test conditions depend on engine data that the
> engine applicant supplies.

## Requirement

The verbs below are CS-29's own. They bind the rotorcraft applicant, not the
engine applicant. See `## Bearing on this engine` for what reaches CS-E.

| Ref | Obligation | Strength |
|---|---|---|
| **(a)** | Perform any additional dynamic, endurance and operational tests, and vibratory investigations, needed to determine that the rotor drive mechanism is safe. | Required |
| **(b)** | Make the test below if turbine engine torque output to the transmission can exceed the highest engine or transmission torque limit, and that output is not directly controlled by the pilot under normal operating conditions. | Required |
| **(b)(1)** | With all engines operating, make 200 applications of torque, each of 10 seconds, at a torque at least equal to the lesser of the two values in (b)(1)(i) and (b)(1)(ii). | Required |
| **(b)(1)(i)** | The first candidate value is the maximum torque used in meeting CS 29.923 plus 10%. | Statement |
| **(b)(1)(ii)** | The second candidate value is the maximum torque attainable under probable operating conditions, assuming that torque limiting devices, if any, function properly. | Statement |
| **(b)(2)** | For a multi-engine rotorcraft, with each engine in turn becoming inoperative, apply to the remaining transmission torque inputs the maximum torque attainable under probable operating conditions, assuming that torque limiting devices, if any, function properly. Test each transmission input at that maximum torque for at least 15 minutes. | Required |
| **(c)** | Sub-points (c)(1) and (c)(2) apply to rotor drive system gearboxes required for continued safe flight or safe landing that have a pressurised normal-use lubrication system. | Statement |
| **(c)(1)** | Category A. Establish confidence that the rotor drive system has an in-flight operational endurance capability of at least 30 minutes after a failure of any one pressurised normal-use lubrication system. | Required |
| **(c)(1)** | Conduct, for each such gearbox, a test simulating the effect of the most severe failure mode of the normal-use lubrication system, as determined by the failure analysis of CS 29.917(b). | Required |
| **(c)(1)** | Make the test duration dependent upon the number of tests and the component condition after the test. | Required |
| **(c)(1)** | Begin the test upon the indication to the flight crew that a lubrication failure has occurred. Load it consistently with 1 minute at maximum continuous power, then the minimum power needed for continued flight at the rotorcraft maximum gross weight. End it with a 45-second out of ground effect (OGE) hover to simulate a landing phase. | Required |
| **(c)(1)** | Substantiate by the test results the maximum period of operation following loss of lubrication, by extended test duration, multiple test specimens, or another approach prescribed by the applicant and accepted by EASA. Support the procedures published in the rotorcraft flight manual (RFM). | Required |
| **(c)(1)** | Flight durations longer than 30 minutes may be demonstrated by a correspondingly longer test, with appropriate margin and substantiation. | Permitted |
| **(c)(2)** | Category B. Establish confidence that the rotor drive system has an in-flight operational endurance capability to complete an autorotation descent and landing after a failure of any one pressurised normal-use lubrication system. | Required |
| **(c)(2)** | Conduct, for each gearbox needed for safe autorotation descent or safe landing, a test of at least 16 minutes and 15 seconds following the most severe failure mode of the normal-use lubrication system, as determined by the failure analysis of CS 29.917(b). | Required |
| **(c)(2)** | Begin the test upon the indication to the flight crew that a lubrication failure has occurred, and load it consistently with 1 minute at maximum continuous power. | Required |
| **(c)(2)** | After that minute, the input torque should be reduced to simulate autorotation for 15 minutes. | Recommended |
| **(c)(2)** | Complete the test by applying an input torque to simulate a minimum power landing for approximately 15 seconds. | Required |
| **(d)** | Subject the rotor drive system to 50 overspeed runs, each 30 ± 3 seconds in duration, at not less than the higher of the rotational speed expected from an engine control device failure or 105% of the maximum rotational speed, including transients, expected in service. | Required |
| **(d)** | The rotational speed limits of speed and torque limiting devices need not be exceeded, where those devices are installed, are independent of the normal engine control, and are shown to be reliable. | Relief |
| **(d)(1)** | Alternate the overspeed runs with stabilising runs of 1 to 5 minutes each, at 60 to 80% of maximum continuous speed. | Required |
| **(d)(2)** | Accomplish acceleration and deceleration in no more than 10 seconds, except where the maximum engine acceleration rate requires more. Do not deduct the time for changing speeds from the specified overspeed run time. | Required |
| **(d)(3)** | Make the overspeed runs with the rotors in the flattest pitch for smooth operation. | Required |
| **(e)** | Conduct the tests of (b) and (d) on the rotorcraft, and absorb the torque by the rotors to be installed. | Required |
| **(e)** | Other ground or flight test facilities with other appropriate methods of torque absorption may be used, if the conditions of support and vibration closely simulate those of a test on the rotorcraft. | Permitted |
| **(f)** | Conduct each test of this paragraph without intervening disassembly. Each part tested must be in a serviceable condition at the conclusion of the test, except for the lubrication system failure test of (c). | Required |

Sub-point (c)(2) uses "should" for the autorotation phase inside an otherwise
mandatory test. CS-29 is a specification, so the verb is a recommendation, not
an accepted means. The surrounding obligations use "shall" and stay mandatory.

Sub-point (d)(2) forbids a deduction: the time spent changing speed "may not be
deducted from the specified time for the overspeed runs" [ext CS 29.927(d)(2)].
The row records that as Required, because the constraint is mandatory.

Category A and Category B are rotorcraft certification categories. They decide
which of (c)(1) and (c)(2) applies. The category is not an engine declaration
and `engine_profile.md` does not carry one.

### Acceptable means — AMC1 29.927, variable rotor speed

| Ref | Obligation | Strength |
|---|---|---|
| **AMC1 29.927(a)** | This AMC supplements FAA AC 29-2C, § AC 29.927, and should be used in conjunction with that AC when demonstrating compliance with CS 29.927. | Accepted method |
| **AMC1 29.927(b)(1)** | A variable rotor speed function allows running at different rotor speed levels, for lower noise or better rotorcraft performance. Beyond the endurance test of CS 29.923, additional tests may be needed to show that a rotor drive system with variable rotor speed is safe. | Statement |
| **AMC1 29.927(b)(2)** | To substantiate acceptable vibration and dynamic behaviour across the available range of rotor speeds, consider performing specific test investigations as prescribed in CS 29.927(a). | Accepted method |
| **AMC1 29.927(b)(2)** | Evaluate the need for representative test runs at the different torque and rotor speed combinations, covering steady states and transient conditions to be encountered in operation, and agree it with the Agency. | Accepted method |

### Acceptable means — AMC1 29.927(c), loss of lubrication

This AMC "replaces item a. (Section 29.927(c)) of FAA AC 29.927 (Amendment
29-26)" [ext AMC1 29.927(c)]. It is the test procedure behind sub-point (c), and
it is the longest single piece of material in this note's subject.

| Ref | Obligation | Strength |
|---|---|---|
| **(a)(1)** | The failure condition to be simulated is the most severe loss of lubrication failure mode of the normal-use lubrication system, defined in AMC2 29.917(b). Assessment of lubrication system reliability is addressed under CS 29.917(b). | Statement |
| **(a)(2)** | CS 29.927(c) is intended to apply to pressurised lubrication systems. The need for dedicated loss of lubrication testing of a gearbox using a non-pressurised splash system is decided by the design assessment of CS 29.917(b). | Statement |
| **(a)(3)** | The provision applies to any pressurised lubrication gearbox necessary for continued safe flight or safe landing. It does not apply to a gearbox that is not essential and whose lubrication system is independent of other essential gearboxes. | Statement |
| **(a)(5)** | The intent for a Category A rotorcraft is confidence in continued flight capability of at least 30 minutes after loss of lubricant pressure in any single gearbox. The rotorcraft flight manual emergency procedures should define the maximum time within which the rotorcraft should land. | Accepted method |
| **(b)(1)** | For a Category B rotorcraft, safe operation under autorotative conditions should be possible for at least 15 minutes. For both categories some damage to rotor drive system components is acceptable after the test, but the condition of the components influences the maximum period of operation. | Accepted method |
| **(c)(1)** | The maximum period of operation following loss of lubrication is the maximum time after a loss of oil pressure warning within which the rotorcraft should land. The period stated in the flight manual should not exceed it. | Statement |
| **(c)(2)** | Residual oil is the oil present in the gearbox after the most severe failure mode, from the time the pilot receives an indication. An auxiliary lubrication system supplements it. | Statement |
| **(d)** | Test each gearbox lubricated by a pressurised system that is necessary for continued safe flight or safe landing. Deviations from the certified configuration may be allowed where needed to install instrumentation or to simulate the most severe failure mode. | Accepted method |
| **(e)(1)(i)** | Start the Category A test at 100 % of the torque associated with all engines operative maximum continuous power, at the nominal speed for use with that power, with the torque for the anti-torque function simulated for straight and level flight, and the oil temperature stabilised at the maximum limit for normal operation. | Accepted method |
| **(e)(1)(ii)** | Drain the oil simulating the most severe failure mode, determined by the failure analysis of CS 29.917(b). Make the location and rate of drainage representative, and continue the drainage throughout the test. | Accepted method |
| **(e)(1)(iii)** | On the low oil pressure warning, continue at all engines operative maximum continuous power for 1 minute. Then reduce torque to at or above the value needed to sustain flight at maximum gross weight at the most efficient flight condition, and hold it for the time the applicant needs to justify the maximum period of operation. Assume the condition starts at 100 % maximum take-off weight, with fuel burn during the test allowed for. | Accepted method |
| **(e)(1)(iv)** | Complete the test by applying power to the gearbox for at least 45 seconds, to simulate an out of ground effect hover. | Accepted method |
| **(e)(1)(v)** | React the input and output shaft torques appropriately and apply the corresponding shaft loads. Apply the vertical load of the main gearbox at the mast, equal to the maximum gross weight of the rotorcraft at 1 g. | Accepted method |
| **(e)(1)(v)** | As the efficiency of the gearbox may change during the test, the input loads may need to be adjusted to maintain the correct output shaft torque. | Statement |
| **(e)(1)(vi)** | The test may be run on a representative bench test rig. | Permitted |
| **(e)(1)(vi)** | Represent all accessory loads by a load associated with normal cruise. Do not run with a test cell ambient temperature below ISA, and use no additional ventilation that could hold the gearbox below the temperatures likely on the helicopter at ISA. | Accepted method |
| **(e)(1)(vii)** | A successful demonstration may involve limited damage, but the gearbox should keep transmitting the necessary torque to the output shafts throughout. Loss of drive to accessories necessary for continued safe flight or safe landing is a test failure. | Accepted method |
| **(e)(2)(i)** | For a Category B rotorcraft the Category A provisions apply, except that the depleted-oil run need only last 15 minutes at a torque and speed simulating autorotative conditions. | Relief |
| **(e)(2)(ii)** | Demonstrating compliance with the Category A provisions is taken to meet the Category B provisions. | Statement |
| **(e)(4)** | Should the applicant wish to establish a positive safety margin for a period longer than 30 minutes, it will be necessary to extend the test duration representing flight at the most efficient flight condition. | Required if claimed |
| **(f)(1)** | Use the duration of the certification test as the starting point, measured from the time the lubrication failure is indicated to the pilot, and reduce it as set out below. | Accepted method |
| **(f)(2)(i)** | Apply a reduction factor of 0.6 where the certification test has no supporting data giving understanding of gearbox behaviour and confidence in repeatability. | Accepted method |
| **(f)(2)(ii)** | Apply 0.8 where the certification test is corroborated by one representative full-scale test showing consistent temperature history and good correlation. | Accepted method |
| **(f)(2)(iii)** | Apply 0.9 where it is corroborated by two or more representative full-scale tests, or by one full-scale test and one or more modular tests, historical data or simulation results, with the behaviour of the limiting design characteristics established and supported by repeatable test data. | Accepted method |
| **(f)(2)(iv)** | Where two or more tests are submitted, treat the shortest as the certification test. Investigate and explain excessive variation between tests. | Accepted method |
| **(f)(3)** | Apply a fixed time penalty for the condition of the components at the end of the test: 2 minutes for CLASS 1, good condition; 5 minutes for CLASS 2, fair condition; 10 minutes for CLASS 3, imminent failure. | Accepted method |
| **(f)(4)** | Calculate the maximum period of operation Td as Td = (Kr × Tc) − Tp. Tc is the certification test duration, from the low-pressure indication to the end of the test; Kr is the reduction factor of (f)(2); Tp is the fixed time penalty of (f)(3). | Accepted method |
| **(f)(5)** | Where a secondary indication is used to raise confidence, show by evidence, preferably from multiple tests, that the monitored failure mode is always the most critical one after a loss of lubrication; justify the availability and reliability of the warning and make it testable at pre-flight or in maintenance. Noise or vibration detected by the crew is not a reliable secondary indication on its own. | Accepted method |
| **(f)(5)(ii)** | If the oil pressure is normal, inhibition of the warning to the flight crew may be considered, to reduce the likelihood of a false warning leading to an instruction to land immediately. | Permitted |

[VERIFY: unlisted construction. Row (e)(1)(v) uses "may need to" and carries
Statement; row (e)(4) uses "will be necessary" and carries Required if claimed.
None of these phrasings is one of the seven source verbs or a listed declaratory
form. The vault reads a possible need as Statement, as it reads "may be
required": nothing is owed until the circumstance arises. The vault reads a
statement of necessity as Required, as it reads "is required to"; a row that
rests on a route the applicant elects takes Required if claimed instead. The
owner decides each construction once, for every row in the vault that carries
it.]

The class criteria in (f)(3) are set out by inspection findings: CLASS 1 parts
are still oil-wetted with little discolouration and at most a slight local
hardness reduction, CLASS 2 parts are almost dry with heavier scuffing and more
hardness loss, and CLASS 3 parts show plastic deformation or local melting. The
gearbox still transmits the required torque in all three.

The explanation in (a)(1) refers to "a capability through testing of at least 36
minutes' duration" [ext AMC1 29.927(c)]. CS 29.927(c)(1) itself asks for an
in-flight endurance capability of at least 30 minutes. The two numbers are not
the same quantity: the formula in (f)(4) converts a test duration into a
demonstrated operating period, and the reduction factor and the time penalty sit
between them.

The design-side companion is AMC2 29.917, the acceptable means for
CS 29.917(b). It defines the most severe failure mode that AMC1 29.927(c) tells
the applicant to simulate. [[CS 29.917]] sets it out in full.

## Bearing on this engine

CS 29.927 creates no CS-E obligation. The tests are run on the rotor drive
system, which is not part of the engine type design. The paragraph still
matters, because three of its test conditions are defined by engine data.

The torque application tests assume the engine's torque limiting devices work.
Both (b)(1)(ii) and (b)(2) set the test torque at "the maximum torque attainable
under probable operating conditions, assuming that torque limiting devices, if
any, function properly" [ext CS 29.927(b)(2)]. Where that limiter is the EECS,
its integrity is engine-side evidence under [[CS-E 50]], and its failure
behaviour reaches the safety analysis of [[CS-E 510]].

The overspeed test takes its speed from an engine failure case. Sub-point (d)
uses "the higher of the rotational speed to be expected from an engine control
device failure or 105% of the maximum rotational speed, including transients, to
be expected in service" [ext CS 29.927(d)]. The first figure comes from the
engine control system assessment, and must reach the installer through the
installation instructions required by [[CS-E 20]].

The OEI case in (b)(2) runs for at least 15 minutes with one engine inoperative.
The torque available from the remaining engines over that period follows from
the ratings declared under [[CS-E 40]], not from the short OEI ratings: 15
minutes exceeds both the 30-Second and the 2-Minute OEI Power Ratings.

[VERIFY: whether the rotorcraft applicant runs the 15-minute input test of
CS 29.927(b)(2) at Continuous OEI torque, or at a higher transient value. CS-29
says only "the maximum torque attainable under probable operating conditions",
and the engine's declared ratings do not settle which condition that is.]

The relief in (d) is engine-dependent in the same way. The rotational speed
limits of speed and torque limiting devices need not be exceeded only where the
devices are "independent of the normal engine control" [ext CS 29.927(d)]. A
full-authority EECS that provides both the control and the limit does not meet
that condition on its own.

Two engine tests resemble these tests but are separate. [CS-E 820] is the
engine Over-torque Test and [CS-E 830] is the Maximum Engine Over-speed test.
Both are run on the engine and prove an engine limit. CS 29.927 proves the
transmission behind it.

The loss-of-lubrication regime in (c) covers the gearbox's own pressurised
lubrication system. It is not the engine Oil System of [CS-E 570], and no CS-E
obligation follows from it.

[VERIFY: whether the installation is certificated under CS-29 or CS-27. The
counterpart paragraph [[CS 27.927]] is materially different, in particular for
loss of lubrication. [[CS-E 30]] carries the same open item.]
